entry.title: Sir Edward Hyde to 'Mr Milles', intercepted letter with code numbers and a cover-name list

entry.title: Duke of Ormond to the Earl of Arran, short passage in code ('a trial whether you are skilful in deciphering')
entry.correspondents: James Butler, 1st Duke of Ormond → Richard Butler, Earl of Arran
entry.shelfmark: HMC, Calendar of the MSS of the Marquess of Ormonde, New Series iv (1906), p. 93 (manuscript shelfmark unknown)
entry.status: Cryptoole XX1678-1 (open). 22 groups in two runs ('726 91 33 425 93 57 384 54 700 720' and '732 573 526 32 643 214 55 440'); the calendar gives no gloss, although it prints Ormond's interlinear decipherments for neighbouring letters (pp. 105-107). Tomokiyo's rejected trial with the Ormond-Longford key is in an HTML comment on charlesii2.htm.
entry.why: Ormond testing his son with a family cipher in the Popish-Plot year; small, but from a well-documented family of reconstructed Ormond keys.
entry.verify: Rebuild the Ormond-Longford 1680 cipher (HMC vol. v pp. 454 ff.) and the Southwell-Ormond 1677-78 code and test them; find the manuscript (Ormonde papers, NLI) for an interlinear gloss HMC did not print.

entry.title: Miguel Fernández Durán to the marqués de San Felipe, envoy at Genoa, despatch in cipher
entry.correspondents: Miguel Fernández Durán (Secretario del Despacho de Guerra) → Vicente Bacallar y Sanna, marqués de San Felipe (Spanish envoy at Genoa)
entry.shelfmark: Barcelona, Archivo de la Corona de Aragón, Diversos, Legación en Génova y Turín, Cajón 1, leg. 22, doc. 67 (DECODE R10181)
entry.status: Cryptoole XX1718-2 (open). DECODE R10181 'Non-decrypted', public access (not public domain). About 309 tokens, 148 distinct (Turner's transcription). The same fonds (Cajón 19, leg. 30) has nine legation keys on DECODE, R10189-R10197 (1711-1718, incl. R10196 of 1718); Turner reports none covers the high values.
entry.why: A war-office despatch to Spain's envoy at Genoa three months after Cape Passaro, during Alberoni's war with the Quadruple Alliance, kept in the legation's own archive with its key sheets.
entry.verify: Pull R10189-R10197 and check each against R10181 (ranges, homophones, two-part arrangement); then search the rest of the Legación en Génova y Turín fonds and AGS Estado/Guerra for the 1718 war-office cipher or a decipherment made at Genoa.

entry.title: Fragments in Girolamo Sirtori's cipher broken by Luis Valle de la Cerda (BNE Mss/994)
entry.correspondents: unknown writer using Girolamo Sirtori's cipher; handed to Luis Valle de la Cerda by a secretary of the Council of State
entry.shelfmark: Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional, Mss/994, ff. 83-90 (ciphertext ff. 85-87); BDH bdh0000174344
entry.status: Cryptoole ITXXXX-1 (partly solved). Valle broke it and said he had devised the same scheme fifteen years earlier; his solution is not extant. Transcription by Sara Gómez Hernández; partial Latin reading by Eloy Caballero (2012) on Cipher Mysteries.

entry.verify: Download ff. 83-90 from BDH, re-transcribe keeping the abbreviation marks, and test Caballero's partial key against a Latin (and Italian/Spanish) model; read ff. 83-84 and 88-90 for Valle's own description of the scheme.
